title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 23
paragraphs: As for Periander, the man who passed word of the oracle to Thrasybulus, he was the son of Cypselus and tyrant of Corinth. During his lifetime, say the Corinthians (and the Lesbians agree with them), there happened to him an extraordinary marvel — namely, that Arion of Methymna was carried ashore at Taenarum on the back of a dolphin. Arion was a harper second to none of his day, and the first, so far as we know, to compose a dithyramb, to give it that name, and to teach it to a chorus at Corinth.
